newsitem.title: BELARUS: Belarus opposition rallies against referendum.
newsitem.headline: Belarus opposition rallies against referendum.

text.p: Up to 5,000 people rallied on Sunday in the Belarus capital of Minsk to protest against a controversial referendum last month that gave sweeping powers to hardline President Alexander Lukashenko.

In the first major public show of opposition to the November 24 referendum which provided Lukashenko with a mandate to rewrite the constitution, an initial crowd of about 2,000 turned up at midday in a central square at the parliament building.

Another 3,000, most of them young, joined the procession when the demonstrators, waving red-and-white national flags and chanting anti-presidential slogans, headed off towards Lukashenko's residence. Police did not interfere.
"We will never accept the falsified constitution," one of the organisers of the rally, Nikolai Statkevich, said.

A summit of the Organisation for Security and Cooperation in Europe (OSCE) said in a statement last week that the referendum "was conducted in contradiction with constitutional procedures and cannot be considered as legitimate".
In a rare and public rebuke to a participating member, it told Lukashenko to ensure the freedom of the media, re-establish full democratic procedures and start talking to the opposition.
Lukashenko, 42, who also attended the summit in Lisbon, shrugged off the criticism and told the 54-nation OSCE not to meddle in his country's affairs.

Within days of the referendum, he took steps to subdue any opposition to his rule. Lukashenko has assembled a lower house composed entirely of his supporters and it promptly passed a law disbanding the old parliament headed by speaker Semyon Sharetsky, symbol of the president's domestic opposition.
Three judges of Belarus's 11-member Constitutional Court, including its head, resigned last week in protest against the referendum.
